findings.issue: Theme system has no SSR-safe hydration — theme class is set client-side after hydration, causing flash-of-unstyled-theme (FOUT)
findings.impact: Users see light theme briefly before dark theme applies on page load; poor perceived performance
findings.fix: Implement SSR-safe theme hydration: read theme preference from cookie on server, inject theme class into <html> before React hydration, suppress hydration warning

findings.issue: Only 2 themes (light/dark) defined via CSS class — no slate dark, OLED high-contrast, or multi-theme token system
findings.impact: Cannot support 4+ named themes without expanding token system to multi-variable per theme pattern
findings.fix: Redesign CSS variable system: define all color tokens per theme (--color-bg-primary, --color-text-primary, etc.), create theme classes (.theme-light, .theme-slate-dark, .theme-oled-black), migrate existing light/dark tokens

findings.issue: Theme toggle only supports system/light/dark — no named theme selection UI
findings.impact: Users cannot choose Slate Dark or OLED High-Contrast themes from preferences
findings.fix: Update theme preferences: add theme selection UI in settings (Light, Slate Dark, OLED Black, System), persist as theme_name in user_preferences table

findings.issue: No automated contrast validation for theme tokens — dark mode and OLED mode contrast not verified
findings.impact: New themes may fail WCAG AA contrast requirements; accessibility regressions
findings.fix: Add automated contrast check in CI: compare all theme token combinations against WCAG AA ratios; fail build on contrast violations

findings.issue: Theme engine supports only light/dark/system; no OLED black or high-contrast accessibility mode
findings.impact: OLED screen users miss battery-saving true-black mode; users with visual impairments lack high-contrast variant.
findings.fix: Add 'oled' and 'high-contrast' resolved theme options with corresponding CSS variable overrides.

findings.issue: No automated WCAG contrast validation or tooling for CSS custom property pairs across themes
findings.impact: Theme token pairs may fail WCAG AA/AAA ratios without detection.
findings.fix: Add CI script to read CSS variable definitions for each theme and validate foreground/background pairs meet WCAG AA thresholds.

findings.issue: Theme switch via classList.add/remove is instant with no CSS transition on custom properties
findings.impact: Users experience an abrupt flash/tear when toggling themes.
findings.fix: Add transition: color 0.2s ease, background-color 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease to :root.

findings.issue: No exposed API for workspace-specific theme overrides (e.g. custom brand colors per workspace)
findings.impact: Workspace admins cannot customize their workspace's color scheme to match company branding.
findings.fix: Add workspace-level CSS variable overrides via a customProperties field on the workspace model.

findings.issue: Reaction routes have no workspace/channel membership check
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can read/add/remove reactions on any message across any workspace
findings.fix: Add requireChannelAccess middleware to GET/POST/DELETE /messages/:id/reactions and GET /reactions/batch

findings.issue: Feature-flag routes have broken middleware — requireWorkspaceMembership("workspaceId") on paths without :workspaceId param
findings.impact: All feature-flag requests will fail with 400 "Missing workspaceId" — feature flags are non-functional
findings.fix: Remove requireWorkspaceMembership from feature-flag routes or add workspaceId as a query/body parameter

findings.issue: Message search uses getSupabase() (anon client) instead of req.supabase (JWT client)
findings.impact: auth.uid() is NULL in SECURITY INVOKER search function — cross-tenant search possible or no results returned
findings.fix: Replace getSupabase() with req.supabase in messages/routes.ts line 38

findings.issue: No Socket.io connection state recovery — clients lose all room state on disconnect
findings.impact: After reconnect, clients must manually re-join rooms and re-fetch state; messages may be lost during disconnect window
findings.fix: Enable connectionStateRecovery in Socket.io server config; implement room membership persistence

findings.issue: No per-event authorization after initial Socket.io auth handshake
findings.impact: Any connected client can join any channel room by emitting channel:join with any channelId
findings.fix: Add per-event membership check in channel:join handler before adding socket to room

findings.issue: In-memory idempotency fallback has no size limit or eviction policy
findings.impact: Unbounded memory growth under high request volume — potential OOM
findings.fix: Add Map size limit with LRU eviction to in-memory fallback

findings.issue: GET /webhooks reads workspace_id from query param but middleware checks req.params — workspace validation broken
findings.impact: Webhook listing bypasses workspace membership check
findings.fix: Create a middleware that reads from req.query.workspace_id instead of req.params.workspaceId

findings.issue: Message upload endpoint has no channel/workspace membership check
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can upload files without channel context
findings.fix: Add channel_id to upload payload and requireChannelAccess middleware

findings.issue: Workspace member list returns email field — PII exposure
findings.impact: Workspace members can see each other's email addresses unnecessarily
findings.fix: Remove email from SELECT query in getMembers(), return only display_name and avatar_url

findings.issue: Channel slug dedup loop has no max attempt safety limit
findings.impact: Infinite loop if all slug variants are taken — potential hang/DoS
findings.fix: Add MAX_ATTEMPTS=100 guard similar to workspace slug dedup

findings.issue: Cursor pagination has no input validation — malformed cursor could cause unexpected query behavior
findings.impact: Malformed cursor could lead to SQL injection-like behavior via .or() filter
findings.fix: Validate cursor format (two parts separated by |) before using in query

findings.issue: Uses console.error instead of structured logger.error for push notification failures
findings.impact: Push notification failures not captured in structured logging; harder to alert/diagnose
findings.fix: Replace console.error with logger.error

findings.issue: Consent routes use lowercase error.message format inconsistent with uppercase error.code convention
findings.impact: Inconsistent API contract — clients must handle two error formats
findings.fix: Standardize consent error responses to use error.code uppercase convention

findings.issue: Idempotency-Key header has no format validation
findings.impact: Any string accepted — potential abuse with very long keys
findings.fix: Add UUID or length validation for idempotency-key header

findings.issue: Reaction add/remove operations emit zero Socket.io events, while every other message mutation broadcasts realtime updates
findings.impact: Users in a channel never see reactions appear or disappear in realtime. Frontend relies on REST polling (GET /reactions/batch) which only fires on new message batches, leaving reaction state stale for up to seconds/minutes.
findings.fix: Add io.to(`channel:${channelId}`).emit('reaction:added', { messageId, reaction }) in reactionService.add() and io.to(`channel:${channelId}`).emit('reaction:removed', { messageId, userId, emoji }) in remove().

findings.issue: presence:update event is never emitted to connected clients despite frontend listening for it
findings.impact: chat-view.tsx registers a listener for presence:update on line 187 but the backend never emits this event. The online count badge remains stuck at 0.
findings.fix: Emit io.emit('presence:update', { total: getOnlineUsers().length }) in socket 'connection' and 'disconnect' handlers. Consider periodic broadcasts every 30s.

findings.issue: Socket reconnect only re-joins channel rooms with no message catch-up mechanism, causing permanent message loss
findings.impact: When a client disconnects (e.g., network blip), on reconnect it emits channel:join but sends no cursor or timestamp for missed messages. Messages sent during the disconnect window are permanently lost.
findings.fix: Track lastKnownMessageId in chat-view state. On reconnect, emit channel:join with a last_seen_message_id parameter. Add server endpoint GET /channels/:id/messages/since?after=<id> to return missed messages.

findings.issue: Channel membership removal has no realtime enforcement — removed users remain in Socket.io rooms until reconnect
findings.impact: When an admin removes a user from a channel, the removed user's active socket connections remain in the channel room, continuing to receive realtime messages for up to 5 minutes.
findings.fix: After removing a member, emit io.to('channel:' + channelId).emit('channel:kick', { userId }) and disconnect that specific user's sockets from the room.

findings.issue: Six instances of .catch(() => {}) silently swallow errors from async side-effects (webhooks, mentions, notifications)
findings.impact: Failures in webhook delivery, @mention resolution, thread reply notifications produce zero log output. Operators cannot detect silent failures.
findings.fix: Replace every .catch(() => {}) with .catch((err) => logger.error('{context} failed', { error: String(err), ...metadata })).

findings.issue: No WebRTC infrastructure at all — no STUN/TURN server configured, no signaling service, no media server choice
findings.impact: Audio/video is a complete greenfield feature requiring new infrastructure and significant architecture decisions
findings.fix: Evaluate media server options: LiveKit (managed/hosted, native WebRTC, SFU architecture), Daily.co (managed, simple API), or mediasoup (self-hosted, flexible). Deploy STUN/TURN server (coturn) for NAT traversal.

findings.issue: No participant media grid component — no video tiles, active speaker detection, or layout management
findings.impact: Core video UI must be built from scratch; no existing patterns in codebase
findings.fix: Design media grid: responsive grid layout (1:1 speaker view, 2x2 for 4 participants, 3x3 for 9+), active speaker highlight with CSS transition, screen share as primary tile when active

findings.issue: No device permission UX — no camera/microphone selector, no permission request flow, no mute/deafen UI
findings.impact: Users cannot control their media devices; no way to mute/unmute or switch cameras
findings.fix: Implement device control bar: mute/unmute mic, camera on/off, screen share, end call; device selector dropdown; browser permission request flow with denied-state handling

findings.issue: No degraded network handling — no bandwidth estimation, no resolution downscaling, no reconnection strategy
findings.impact: Poor network conditions will cause frozen video, missing audio, or dropped calls with no user feedback
findings.fix: Implement bandwidth estimation and adaptive resolution (simulcast/SVC); add reconnection logic with visual indicator; display 'poor connection' warning

findings.issue: No keyboard shortcuts or accessibility for media controls — mute/deafen hotkeys, screen reader announcements for participant activity
findings.impact: Media controls inaccessible to keyboard-only users; participant changes not announced to screen readers
findings.fix: Add keyboard shortcuts (M=mic mute, D=deafen, Ctrl+E=end call); add aria-live region for participant joined/left announcements; ensure focus management in media grid

findings.issue: No WebRTC test strategy — media testing requires special infrastructure
findings.impact: Audio/video reliability cannot be validated in standard CI
findings.fix: Write Playwright tests using fake media devices (chrome --use-fake-device-for-media-stream); test UI state transitions, device selection, mute/unmute; use LiveKit's built-in E2E test framework if using LiveKit

findings.issue: MediaRoom only shows generic 'Failed to connect to media server' on error with no distinction between permission-denied, network failure, or LiveKit unavailability
findings.impact: When browser blocks camera/mic, users see a vague error with no guidance to check browser permissions.
findings.fix: Catch getUserMedia errors specifically: check for NotAllowedError and show contextual message with link to browser permission settings.

findings.issue: Dev remote compose omits LIVEKIT_HOST env var on API container, breaking LiveKit token generation in development
findings.impact: Developers testing media features locally must manually add LIVEKIT_HOST to .env because devremote compose does not pass it.
findings.fix: Add LIVEKIT_HOST: http://livekit:7880 to API environment in docker-compose.devremote.yml.

findings.issue: MediaRoom uses ControlBar variation='minimal' which hides screen share and other advanced controls
findings.impact: Users cannot share their screen during calls unless the minimal variant exposes it.
findings.fix: Add a dedicated screen-share toggle button outside ControlBar, or switch to variation='full'.

findings.issue: No keyboard shortcut support for media controls — mute/unmute (M), video toggle (V), screen share (S), leave call (Esc)
findings.impact: Users cannot quickly mute/unmute or toggle video during calls via keyboard, which is standard in all major video conferencing tools.
findings.fix: Add global keydown event listeners in MediaRoom for M (mute), V (toggle video), S (screen share), Esc (minimize/leave).

findings.issue: No backup strategy for Supabase Storage files (chat-uploads bucket — avatars and file uploads)
findings.impact: All user-uploaded content (avatars, shared files) has zero backup — complete data loss if storage bucket is corrupted or deleted
findings.fix: Create script to export Supabase Storage bucket to DO Spaces or S3 on a schedule; document restore procedure

findings.issue: No restore test evidence exists — no documented restore drill procedure, no scripts, no evidence of any restore being tested
findings.impact: Backup may be non-functional or incomplete; first restore attempt will be during a real outage
findings.fix: Write and execute a quarterly restore drill; document procedure; create restore script

findings.issue: RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective) not defined anywhere in the codebase
findings.impact: No recovery expectations documented — operators cannot determine if recovery is 'fast enough'
findings.fix: Define RTO (e.g., 4 hours) and RPO (e.g., 1 hour) based on business requirements; document in runbook

findings.issue: No dedicated backup runbook in docs/runbooks/ — Supabase PITR mentioned only in passing in migration runbook
findings.impact: Operators lack step-by-step backup/restore guidance during incident
findings.fix: Create docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md with: Supabase PITR procedure, storage bucket export, full DR (droplet loss) recovery

findings.issue: No automated Supabase backup verification — no script to check that daily Supabase backup completed successfully
findings.impact: Backup failures go unnoticed until restore is attempted — worst-case: no valid backup exists
findings.fix: Add daily cron job or GitHub scheduled workflow to check Supabase backup status via API

findings.issue: No pg_dump or Supabase export scripts exist — only relies on Supabase managed backups
findings.impact: No offline backup available if Supabase service is unavailable
findings.fix: Add scripts/pg_dump.sh or scripts/export-supabase.sh for on-demand or scheduled export

findings.issue: No full disaster recovery runbook covering total droplet loss scenario
findings.impact: If the DO droplet is lost, operators must reconstruct recovery steps from multiple scattered documents
findings.fix: Create full DR runbook: Terraform init -> apply -> restore DB via PITR -> restore storage -> smoke test

findings.issue: Docker HEALTHCHECK succeeded but no application-level smoke test after restore
findings.impact: Restore can pass health check while critical features are still broken (auth, messaging, realtime)
findings.fix: Add smoke test step to restore runbook: verify auth flow, message send, WebSocket connect, file access

findings.issue: Terraform state has no DR backup plan — DO Spaces bucket has no cross-region replication configured
findings.impact: If DO Spaces bucket is lost, Terraform state is unrecoverable — infrastructure must be rebuilt from scratch
findings.fix: Document Terraform state recovery: import existing resources from cloud provider; consider state bucket replication

findings.issue: No backup scripts exist in the repository — zero pg_dump, Supabase export, or storage backup scripts
findings.impact: Production data relies entirely on Supabase managed backups with no verification or export mechanism. No offline backup to restore from.
findings.fix: Create scripts/pg_dump.sh for on-demand PostgreSQL dumps; create scripts/export-supabase-storage.sh for storage bucket mirroring; add scheduled GitHub workflow for daily exports.

findings.issue: No dedicated backup/restore runbook — restore procedures are scattered across migration and incident runbooks
findings.impact: Operators have no single authoritative document for full disaster recovery, database PITR, storage bucket restore, or tenant-scoped recovery.
findings.fix: Create docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md covering: daily backup verification, PITR procedure, storage bucket export/import, full DR scenario, RTO/RPO commitments.

findings.issue: Supabase Storage files (avatars, file uploads) have no backup coverage
findings.impact: All user-uploaded content exists only in Supabase Storage with no export or backup. Storage bucket corruption or compromise results in permanent data loss.
findings.fix: Add scheduled export script copying Supabase Storage bucket to DO Spaces using Supabase Management API or S3-compatible copy.

findings.issue: No automated backup integrity verification — Supabase managed backup status is never checked
findings.impact: Backup failures go undetected until a restore is attempted, potentially during a real disaster with no valid backup.
findings.fix: Add scheduled GitHub workflow (daily) checking Supabase backup status via Management API. Include row count parity check against key tables.

findings.issue: No DB query timeouts on any Supabase query across all 15+ service files. queryWithTimeout() helper exists at lib/db-timeout.ts but is never imported or used.
findings.impact: Any slow DB query (unindexed search, lock contention, DB overload) will hang the HTTP request indefinitely. Connection pool starvation cascades to all routes. Complete API outage on DB degradation.
findings.fix: Apply queryWithTimeout() or AbortSignal.timeout to all supabase.from().select()/.update()/.insert()/.delete() calls in all service files

findings.issue: No idempotency keys on workspace, channel, reaction, webhook create, member add/remove, or push subscription mutations - only message.create has idempotency
findings.impact: Duplicate requests from network retry cause duplicate resources. Users may create multiple workspaces, channels, or reactions from a single intent.
findings.fix: Add idempotency-key header checking to all POST mutation endpoints

findings.issue: 14 silent .catch(() => {}) blocks across the codebase - webhook trigger calls, cache operations, notification creation, socket events all swallow errors
findings.impact: Critical failures in webhook delivery, notification creation, and cache operations are completely invisible. No logging, no metrics, no user feedback.
findings.fix: Replace all .catch(() => {}) with .catch(err => logger.error({ err, context: '...' }, 'Operation failed')) in every catch block

findings.issue: Push notification delivery has no circuit breaker protection
findings.impact: A failing push notification service (e.g. VAPID endpoint slow or unreachable) will cascade failures across all push notification attempts, with no fail-fast mechanism.
findings.fix: Wrap push notification delivery in a circuit breaker (using existing lib/circuit-breaker.ts with per-endpoint keys)

findings.issue: Worker has no BullMQ queue/worker drain on SIGTERM - active jobs may be abruptly terminated
findings.impact: Jobs in progress during shutdown are lost without visibility. No graceful completion or re-queue of in-flight work.
findings.fix: Call worker.close() and queue.drain() in the SIGTERM handler before process.exit

findings.issue: No DNS resolution timeout in webhook URL validation - dns.resolve4() call has no timeout
findings.impact: Slow DNS resolution (misconfigured nameserver, network issue) holds the request open indefinitely. Hangs webhook validation.
findings.fix: Add AbortSignal.timeout to dns.resolve4() call with a 5s timeout

findings.issue: queryWithTimeout() utility for Supabase queries with configurable timeout exists but is never used anywhere in the codebase
findings.impact: Dead code that creates a false sense of security. Engineers may assume timeouts are in place when they are not.
findings.fix: Either integrate into all service files or remove the unused utility to avoid confusion

findings.issue: Circuit breaker stats (getCircuitBreakerStats) exist but are not exposed via any API endpoint - operators cannot query circuit states without SSH
findings.impact: When circuit breakers trip, operators have no way to inspect which endpoints are open without direct server access. Delays incident response.
findings.fix: Expose circuit breaker stats via an admin endpoint (GET /admin/circuit-breakers with admin auth)

findings.issue: Chat app shares Tailwind CSS configuration strategy with MCT Portal (both use Tailwind v4 with @theme directive) but no shared theme package exists
findings.impact: Theme changes must be duplicated across projects; design token drift between Chat and Portal
findings.fix: Create shared @chat/theme package with common design tokens; both apps import from shared package

findings.issue: Chat app uses same Supabase project pattern as Portal but has separate migrations — potential schema conflicts if both apps access same Supabase project
findings.impact: Table naming conflicts; RLS policy overlaps; accidental cross-app data access
findings.fix: Verify Chat and Portal use separate Supabase projects; if shared, add table name prefixing (chat_) and separate RLS policies

findings.issue: Chat app uses pnpm workspace monorepo with packages/ shared across apps — but Portal may have its own versions of similar packages
findings.impact: Duplicate implementations of Button, Input, Dialog, etc. between Chat and Portal; no shared UI component library
findings.fix: Audit @chat/ui components vs Portal equivalents; extract shared components to @mct/ui package

findings.issue: Chat app uses same-domain /v1/* proxy architecture for API; Portal may use direct subdomain or different pattern
findings.impact: Integration between Chat and Portal requires consistent API routing strategy
findings.fix: Document API routing architecture decision; align with Portal if integration is planned

findings.issue: Chat app uses Socket.io for real-time; Portal likely uses different WebSocket approach
findings.impact: Cross-app real-time communication (Portal notifications about Chat activity) requires bridge
findings.fix: Design cross-app event bus (Redis pub/sub or NATS) if Chat and Portal need real-time integration

findings.issue: Chat app includes Sentry-instrumented error boundaries; Portal likely has similar instrumentation
findings.impact: Potential Sentry DSN/org duplication; separate error tracking silos
findings.fix: Consolidate Sentry projects under single org; share DSN naming convention

findings.issue: Chat app version badge shows branch+SHA+build date; Portal version scheme unknown
findings.impact: Inconsistent version identification across products
findings.fix: Standardize version badge format across Chat and Portal; share version utility

findings.issue: [Phase A] Message stream renders all messages as flat DOM — no virtualization, no inverted scroll, no scroll anchoring
findings.impact: Channels with 1000+ messages freeze browser; new messages push scrolled-up position
findings.fix: Virtualize message list with @tanstack/react-virtual; implement inverted scroll; add scroll anchoring via IntersectionObserver

findings.issue: [Phase C] Composer is a plain <textarea> — no markdown preview, no @mention autocomplete, no emoji picker, no drag-drop file upload
findings.impact: Core composing experience is primitive; users cannot use modern chat interaction patterns
findings.fix: Implement rich composer: markdown preview toggle, @mention popover with debounced search, emoji picker triggered by : or button, drag-drop zone with upload progress, Ctrl+B/I for bold/italic

findings.issue: [Phase A] No message grouping date separators or time-based grouping — all messages shown as flat continuous list
findings.impact: Users cannot quickly identify when messages were sent; no visual temporal navigation
findings.fix: Add date separator headers ('Today', 'Yesterday', 'Monday', 'June 15') between message groups; group messages by time proximity (within 5 minutes = same group)

findings.issue: [Phase B] Thread panel shows replies without parent message context — users must remember or scroll to find parent
findings.impact: Thread context is lost; users cannot see what message is being replied to without navigating away
findings.fix: Sticky parent message preview at top of thread panel: truncated content, author avatar, timestamp, clickable link to parent in channel

findings.issue: [Phase B] No thread indicator on messages — no reply count badge, last reply preview, or thread activity indicator
findings.impact: Users cannot see which messages have active threads without clicking each message
findings.fix: Add thread reply count badge (e.g., '3 replies') below message; show last reply preview text on hover; highlight messages with unread thread replies

findings.issue: [Phase C] No draft persistence for messages — composing a long message and navigating away loses content
findings.impact: Users lose unsent messages on navigation or accidental refresh; no recovery
findings.fix: Save message draft to localStorage per channel+thread; restore on compose focus; show draft indicator ('Draft: ...') in channel list

findings.issue: [Phase A] Message actions (reply, react, edit, delete) hidden on hover — opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100
findings.impact: Touch users cannot access message actions; keyboard users must tab to each message
findings.fix: Show actions on group-focus-within for keyboard; always visible on touch devices; minimum 44x44px touch targets

findings.issue: [Phase D] Typing indicator not throttled server-side — only client-side throttle at 2000ms
findings.impact: Rapid typing changes fire many events; no server protection against flooding
findings.fix: Add server-side rate limiting for typing:start (max 1 per 2s per user per channel); keep client throttle as defense-in-depth

findings.issue: [Phase D] Connection banner shows 'Connecting...' but no reconnection progress or ETA
findings.impact: Users see generic message during disconnect with no indication of recovery
findings.fix: Add reconnection progress: spinner animation, elapsed time, 'Still trying...' after 10s, 'Connection lost' after 30s with manual retry button

findings.issue: [Phase E] No mobile bottom action bar — message actions require long-press or scrolling back to header
findings.impact: Mobile chat has no quick-action bar for common operations (search, notifications, recent mentions)
findings.fix: Add mobile bottom action bar: compose FAB button, unread badge, notification bell, search icon; floating over message list

findings.issue: [Phase E] Thread panel on mobile is full-screen overlay with no back-navigation to channel context
findings.impact: Mobile thread traps users; no way to see channel while reading thread
findings.fix: Mobile thread: full-screen view with back arrow returning to channel at preserved scroll position; swipe-right gesture to go back

findings.issue: [Phase A] System messages (user joined, channel created, message pinned) not visually distinguished from user messages
findings.impact: System events blend with user content; hard to scan for actual conversation
findings.fix: Style system messages with reduced opacity, smaller font, italic text, no avatar — visually distinct from user messages

findings.issue: [Phase D] No 'Jump to present' button when scrolled up — users must manually scroll to bottom
findings.impact: Inconvenient to return to latest messages after reviewing history
findings.fix: Add floating 'Jump to present' FAB button with # new messages count; click scrolls smoothly to latest with animation

findings.issue: [Phase E] Message selection on mobile is accidental — no haptic feedback or visual selection indicator
findings.impact: Users may accidentally trigger message actions while scrolling on mobile
findings.fix: Add haptic feedback (navigator.vibrate) on message action trigger; add 300ms long-press threshold before showing action menu

findings.issue: Chat UI dark mode broken - .dark class applied by ThemeProvider but CSS only matches @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)
findings.impact: Chat background, message bubbles, input field, and sidebar all use wrong color scheme when user manually toggles theme. Chat becomes unreadable in some theme/OS combinations.
findings.fix: Add .dark selector support to CSS variables for all chat-related components

findings.issue: Thread replies lack edit, delete, and reaction support - read-only after sending
findings.impact: Phase B (thread UX) incomplete. Users cannot correct mistakes in thread replies, cannot remove unwanted replies, and cannot react to replies. Major UX gap vs Discord/Slack.
findings.fix: Add edit action (PUT /messages/:id), delete action (DELETE /messages/:id with confirmation), and reaction support to thread panel

findings.issue: No per-user online/offline presence indicators anywhere in the UI
findings.impact: Phase D (presence) incomplete. Users cannot determine if other users are online. Only an aggregate 'N online' count is shown.
findings.fix: Add per-user green/gray dot indicator next to user names in message list, thread panel, and member surfaces

findings.issue: Typing indicator shows only count ('2 people are typing...') never shows individual names
findings.impact: Users cannot tell who is typing. When only one person is typing, showing 'Someone is typing...' instead of their name reduces chat awareness.
findings.fix: Show names for 1-2 typists, fall back to count only for 3+ (e.g. 'Alice is typing...' / 'Alice and Bob are typing...')

findings.issue: No slash commands support (/giphy, /poll, /me, /shrug, etc.)
findings.impact: Phase C (composer) incomplete. Users expect slash commands as a power-user feature for quick actions. Competitors like Slack and Discord rely heavily on slash commands.
findings.fix: Add slash command parser with command menu popover. Start with /me for action messages and /poll for quick polls.

findings.issue: Reaction picker limited to 6 emojis - no full emoji palette available
findings.impact: Users can only react with 6 preset emojis. Cannot express nuanced reactions. Competitors offer full emoji pickers.
findings.fix: Add full emoji picker (e.g. emoji-mart or data-minecraft) to the reaction button in addition to the 6 quick emojis

findings.issue: No reaction tooltip/popover showing who reacted with which emoji
findings.impact: Users see reaction counts but cannot see who reacted. Reduces social awareness and makes it hard to know who agreed/disagreed.
findings.fix: Add hover/click tooltip on reaction pills showing user avatars/names who reacted

findings.issue: No pinned or bookmarked message support
findings.impact: Phase A (message stream) lacks common feature for important message retention. Users cannot pin messages for channel reference.
findings.fix: Implement message pinning with a pinned messages bar in the channel header

findings.issue: Cloudflare origin cert and private key written to disk via echo heredoc — multi-line secrets can appear in GitHub Actions logs if shell fails
findings.impact: TLS private key and origin certificate could be exposed in CI logs, compromising TLS security for the production domain
findings.fix: Use GitHub Actions secrets directly in environment files ($GITHUB_ENV), or write secrets to files using GitHub Actions file commands

findings.issue: CI/CD secrets injected into .env files via inline echo commands — shell parsing errors can expose secrets in build logs
findings.impact: Multiple secrets (Supabase keys, VAPID keys) could appear in CI logs if shell expansion fails
findings.fix: Use env: block in docker compose or GitHub Actions environment files; avoid echo-based secret injection

findings.issue: Workflows do not declare explicit GITHUB_TOKEN permissions — defaulting to write-all broad permissions
findings.impact: If a workflow is compromised (e.g., via malicious PR), the GITHUB_TOKEN has write access to all repository resources
findings.fix: Add explicit permissions: block to every workflow: contents: read, issues: read, pull-requests: read, actions: read

findings.issue: No production approval gate — push to main or workflow_dispatch immediately deploys to production without manual approval step
findings.impact: Any code merged to main or anyone with dispatch access can deploy to production with zero human review
findings.fix: Add environment: production with required reviewers to the deploy job; add 'prod-approval' environment protection rule in GitHub

findings.issue: GitHub branch protection rules are not actually enforced — validate.yml only read-checks but doesn't apply them; no required status checks on main
findings.impact: PRs can merge to main without passing lint, tests, or audit gates; no CI enforcement at all
findings.fix: Configure branch protection via Terraform github_branch_protection resource or GitHub API; add audit-gate as required check

findings.issue: GITHUB_TOKEN piped to docker login via echo — full token exposed in SSH session commands
findings.impact: GITHUB_TOKEN with write:packages scope visible in SSH history; could be harvested from compromised droplet
findings.fix: Pass GITHUB_TOKEN as environment variable to SSH script instead of inlining in command

findings.issue: deploy-production.yml triggers on any push to main — no path filtering to ensure only relevant changes trigger a production deploy
findings.impact: A README change to main triggers a full production deploy with image build, SSH, and container restart
findings.fix: Add paths filter to deploy-production.yml trigger: paths: ['apps/', 'packages/', 'infra/', 'supabase/', 'scripts/']

findings.issue: No artifact retention policy documented — build artifacts use GitHub Actions defaults (90 days)
findings.impact: Build artifacts with potentially sensitive intermediate data retained unnecessarily
findings.fix: Set artifact retention to 7 days for CI builds, 30 days for release builds; document retention policy

findings.issue: 81 secrets interpolated inline in run: script blocks across 3 deploy workflows (deploy-development.yml, deploy-production.yml, infra-development.yml) - secrets visible in process listings and logs
findings.impact: CI secrets (DO_API_TOKEN, CI_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, CF_ORIGIN_CERT, etc.) exposed via shell command argument interpolation. Any process on the runner can read them via /proc. GitHub may redact but cannot prevent runtime exposure.
findings.fix: Move all secrets to env: blocks and reference via environment variables in shell scripts. Never use ${{ secrets.X }} inside run: strings.

findings.issue: 16 of 19 workflows lack explicit permissions: blocks - GITHUB_TOKEN defaults to write-all scope
findings.impact: If any workflow is compromised (e.g. via dependency confusion, malicious PR), the GITHUB_TOKEN has write access to contents, issues, pull_requests, actions, and more. Unnecessary blast radius.
findings.fix: Add explicit permissions: blocks to all 16 workflows, scoped to minimum required (e.g. contents: read, packages: write for build workflows)

findings.issue: deploy-production.yml triggers on ANY push to main branch - no path filters to limit production deploys to relevant changes
findings.impact: Documentation-only changes, README edits, or other non-code pushes trigger a full production build + deploy cycle. Wasteful and increases deployment risk window.
findings.fix: Add paths: filters to deploy-production.yml triggers (apps/api/**, apps/web/**, packages/**, infra/docker/**, .github/workflows/deploy-production.yml)

findings.issue: validate.yml has a fallback hardcoded anon key string that resembles a real Supabase anon key
findings.impact: If the SUPABASE_ANON_KEY secret is empty, the workflow falls back to a potentially real-looking key in plaintext. Minor but unnecessary risk.
findings.fix: Remove the hardcoded fallback string, use a clearly fake placeholder (e.g. 'placeholder-key') or fail the workflow if the secret is missing

findings.issue: Workspace slug dedup loop in workspaces service has no max-attempt guard — while(true) can hang forever
findings.impact: If all slug variants are taken (e.g., 'workspace-1' through 'workspace-100'), the loop spins indefinitely — potential DoS
findings.fix: Add MAX_ATTEMPTS=100 counter and throw error after exhausting attempts — already done in workspaces/service.ts but CHECK channels/service.ts has NO safeguard

findings.issue: No optimistic locking on any PATCH handler — no If-Match header, no version column, no checkVersionMatch pattern
findings.impact: Concurrent edits silently overwrite each other — last writer wins with no conflict detection
findings.fix: Add version column (INT DEFAULT 1) to messages, workspaces, channels tables; implement If-Match header check in PATCH handlers; return 409 on version mismatch

findings.issue: webhook_endpoints.created_by FK has no ON DELETE action — defaults to RESTRICT
findings.impact: Deleting an auth user who created webhooks will fail with FK violation; user deletion cascading is blocked
findings.fix: Add ON DELETE SET NULL or ON DELETE CASCADE to the FK constraint

findings.issue: TypeScript types severely out of sync with DB schema — 6 interfaces defined vs 16 tables; soft-delete fields missing from Workspace/Channel/Message types
findings.impact: Type-safety gaps across codebase; developers must use 'any' for non-existent types; schema drift goes undetected
findings.fix: Run supabase gen types typescript --local > packages/db/src/types.ts; add CI check for type-schema drift

findings.issue: Soft-delete on workspaces/channels/messages does not cascade soft-delete to child records (channel_members, messages in workspace, reactions on soft-deleted messages)
findings.impact: Orphaned channel_members point to deleted channels; reactions on soft-deleted messages remain; workspace soft-delete leaves all channels/messages undeleted
findings.fix: Add trigger to cascade soft-delete: workspace soft-delete -> soft-delete all channels -> soft-delete all messages; channel soft-delete -> soft-delete all messages

findings.issue: Missing index on reactions.message_id — all reaction queries filter by message_id but no index exists
findings.impact: Full table scans on every reaction fetch; O(n) per message on reaction-heavy channels
findings.fix: CREATE INDEX idx_reactions_message_id ON public.reactions(message_id)

findings.issue: Workspace creation is multi-table (workspaces + workspace_members + webhook trigger) but NOT wrapped in a DB transaction
findings.impact: If workspace_members insert succeeds but subsequent operations fail, partial state exists — orphan workspace or missing member records
findings.fix: Wrap workspace creation in Supabase RPC with BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, or use application-level compensating actions

findings.issue: Missing composite index on channel_members (channel_id, user_id) — private channel access checks use this pair
findings.impact: Slow channel access checks on private channels with many members
findings.fix: CREATE INDEX idx_channel_members_channel_user ON public.channel_members(channel_id, user_id)

findings.issue: No down/rollback scripts for any of 26 migrations — forward-fix is only recovery path
findings.impact: Schema rollback requires PITR with data loss; no automated way to reverse a migration
findings.fix: Write .down.sql scripts for all 26 migrations; mandate down scripts in migration template

findings.issue: No optimistic locking on ANY PATCH handler - all 9 use last-write-wins. No version column, If-Match header, or ETag comparison anywhere.
findings.impact: Two users simultaneously editing the same message, workspace, channel, or webhook will silently overwrite each other's changes. Data loss on concurrent edits guaranteed.
findings.fix: Add version column to all mutable entities, require If-Match header on PATCH, return 409 Conflict on version mismatch

findings.issue: GDPR DELETE /account performs 8 sequential deletes without transaction wrapping - partial deletion if any step fails
findings.impact: If deletion fails mid-way (e.g. after removing messages but before removing the user), the user is left with dangling references and can't retry. Data integrity violation.
findings.fix: Wrap all deletion operations in a Supabase RPC transaction with BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK

findings.issue: webhook_endpoints.created_by FK references auth.users(id) with NO ON DELETE clause - defaults to NO ACTION
findings.impact: Deleting an auth user who created webhook endpoints will fail with foreign key violation. Orphan blocking delete.
findings.fix: Add ON DELETE SET NULL or ON DELETE CASCADE to the webhook_endpoints.created_by FK

findings.issue: API services use hard DELETE instead of calling soft-delete functions that exist in migrations (soft_delete_workspace, soft_delete_channel, etc.)
findings.impact: Deleted workspaces, channels, and messages are permanently lost with no recovery option. Soft-delete infrastructure exists but is bypassed.
findings.fix: Replace .delete() calls with .update({ deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() }) or RPC calls to soft-delete functions

findings.issue: No transaction coverage on multi-table writes - message creation, webhook delivery, notification creation are fire-and-forget with no rollback safety
findings.impact: Message inserted but webhook trigger or mention notification may fail silently. No atomicity guarantee for any write operation spanning multiple tables.
findings.fix: Use Supabase RPC functions with BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK for multi-table write operations

findings.issue: All 6 data retention/purge/archive pg_cron.schedule calls are commented out. Worker cleanup processor is a no-op with TODO comments.
findings.impact: Audit logs, notifications, consent logs, old messages, and webhook deliveries accumulate indefinitely. Unbounded table growth degrades query performance over time.
findings.fix: Enable pg_cron extension and uncomment cron.schedule calls. Implement cleanup logic in worker/src/processors/cleanup.ts

findings.issue: notification_preferences table is created with trigger-based defaults but has no API endpoints to read or write them
findings.impact: Data is written but never queried from the API. Preferences cannot be managed by users despite the settings UI having toggles for them.
findings.fix: Add API endpoints for notification preferences CRUD, or remove the table if superseded by user_preferences

findings.issue: 4 database tables are missing TypeScript types: thread_metadata, thread_participants, channel_role_overrides, notification_preferences
findings.impact: TypeScript code using these tables has implicit 'any' types. Runtime errors from type mismatches not caught at compile time. Drift between schema and types.
findings.fix: Add type definitions for all 4 missing tables to packages/db/src/types.ts

findings.issue: SECURITY DEFINER functions missing SET search_path — 4 functions affected
findings.impact: Search_path injection attack: user-created objects can hijack elevated privileges
findings.fix: Add SET search_path = 'public' to handle_new_user(), handle_new_channel(), handle_new_workspace(), and the fixed version in migration 22

findings.issue: Missing INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE RLS policies for workspace_members and channel_members tables
findings.impact: Direct user operations on member tables bypass RLS — relies entirely on application-level middleware
findings.fix: Add INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies for workspace_members and channel_members with auth.uid() checks

findings.issue: TypeScript types significantly out of sync with database schema — 6 types defined vs 16 tables exist
findings.impact: Type safety gaps: developers referencing missing types will fall back to any; soft-delete fields (deleted_at, archived_at) missing from Workspace, Channel, Message types
findings.fix: Run npx supabase gen types typescript --local > packages/db/src/types.ts; verify all tables represented

findings.issue: Migration sequence gap in 20260626 batch — jumps from 01 to 22 with 21 missing sequence numbers
findings.impact: Suggests migrations were deleted or renumbered; Supabase CLI tracking by filename may conflict
findings.fix: Audit migration sequence; create placeholder files or renumber to eliminate gaps

findings.issue: Webhook_endpoints.created_by FK has no ON DELETE action — defaults to RESTRICT
findings.impact: Deleting an auth user who created webhooks will fail with FK violation
findings.fix: Add ON DELETE SET NULL or ON DELETE CASCADE to webhook_endpoints.created_by FK constraint

findings.issue: Runbook incorrectly states 'PostgreSQL does not support transactional DDL rollback'
findings.impact: Misguided operator guidance — DDL inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK IS supported, preventing safe rollback
findings.fix: Correct the runbook: PostgreSQL fully supports DDL rollback within transaction blocks

findings.issue: Missing index on reactions.message_id — all reaction queries filter by message_id
findings.impact: Full table scans on reaction queries for channels with many messages and reactions
findings.fix: CREATE INDEX idx_reactions_message_id ON public.reactions(message_id)

findings.issue: Missing index on notifications.workspace_id — workspace-level notification queries
findings.impact: Full table scans for workspace notification listing
findings.fix: CREATE INDEX idx_notifications_workspace_id ON public.notifications(workspace_id)

findings.issue: Seed data contains plaintext webhook secrets visible in repository
findings.impact: Development secrets committed to git — if repository access is compromised, secrets are exposed
findings.fix: Remove hardcoded secrets from seed files; use placeholder values like 'CHANGE_ME'

findings.issue: No down/rollback scripts exist for any of the 26 migrations
findings.impact: Rollback requires manual SQL construction per incident or PITR with data loss
findings.fix: Write .down.sql reversal scripts for each migration, starting with the last 5 additive-column migrations

findings.issue: Dual migration application paths: supabase db execute (dev scripts) vs supabase db push (CI)
findings.impact: Different code paths may produce different results — db push uses migration tracking, db execute runs raw SQL
findings.fix: Standardize on supabase db push for all environments; remove db execute fallback path

findings.issue: Message interface declares archived_at field but no migration ever adds this column to the messages table
findings.impact: TypeScript `Message` type has `archived_at: string | null` but no migration adds the column. At runtime, `data as Message` produces `undefined` for `archived_at`, causing logic errors in archival workflows.
findings.fix: Add migration: ALTER TABLE public.messages ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ; OR remove archived_at from the TypeScript type.

findings.issue: Reactions table SELECT RLS policy is USING (true), granting any authenticated user access to all reactions across all workspaces
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can enumerate reactions for any message regardless of workspace or channel membership, leaking message IDs and reaction patterns in private channels.
findings.fix: Replace with membership-scoped policy joining through messages, channels, and workspace_members.

findings.issue: Circular RLS dependency between channels and channel_role_overrides required three hotfix migrations (006, 007, 008) — final state removes override check from channels entirely
findings.impact: Migration 006 introduced circular RLS dependency causing infinite recursion. Final state (008) removed override check from channels SELECT entirely, making the override table inert for hiding channels.
findings.fix: Re-integrate channel_role_overrides into channel SELECT policy via SECURITY DEFINER helper that breaks circular dependency, or remove the table entirely.

findings.issue: Message deletion uses hard DELETE despite full soft-delete infrastructure being built and deployed
findings.impact: Migration 014 built soft-delete infrastructure (deleted_at column, RLS filtering, restore functions) but the API still uses hard DELETE. Deleted messages cannot be recovered by admins.
findings.fix: Change to UPDATE messages SET deleted_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1. Add PATCH /messages/:id/restore endpoint (admin-only) calling existing restore_message() function.

findings.issue: No index on messages.parent_id, causing full table scans for thread reply listing and the thread_metadata trigger
findings.impact: Thread queries SELECT * FROM messages WHERE parent_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at ASC. Neither existing index covers this pattern. Each thread view performs a sequential scan.
findings.fix: Add migration: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_parent_id ON public.messages(parent_id) WHERE parent_id IS NOT NULL;

findings.issue: No request timeout on any Supabase query — slow DB can block Node event loop indefinitely, causing complete API outage
findings.impact: 30s DB query latency blocks all request threads; entire API becomes unresponsive; no circuit breaker to give recovery time
findings.fix: Add AbortSignal.timeout(10000) to all Supabase queries; wrap Supabase client in circuit breaker

findings.issue: Socket.io has no connection state recovery — clients lose all room memberships on reconnect; no offline message queue
findings.impact: Messages sent during disconnect window are lost; after reconnect, clients must manually re-join each channel
findings.fix: Enable connectionStateRecovery; implement client-side reconnection with exponential backoff; add message queue flush on reconnect

findings.issue: No global error boundary around workspace/channel content — uncaught React errors show blank page with no recovery action
findings.impact: Any unhandled React error in chat components results in a completely blank UI; user must manually refresh
findings.fix: Add ErrorBoundary wrapper with 'Try Again' button around chat content area

findings.issue: Webhook GET route reads workspace_id from query param but middleware reads req.params — query param never checked for authorization
findings.impact: Webhook listing endpoint bypasses workspace membership validation
findings.fix: Add query parameter reading middleware or move workspace_id to route param

findings.issue: Push notification delivery failures use console.error instead of structured logger.error
findings.impact: Push failures invisible in centralized logging; no ability to alert on failure rates
findings.fix: Replace console.error with logger.error including structured context (notification type, user agent, error code)

findings.issue: Cloudflare origin cert and private key written to disk via echo heredoc in CI/CD — secret exposure risk
findings.impact: TLS private key could appear in CI logs on shell failure; compromises TLS security for production domain
findings.fix: Use GitHub Actions env file ($GITHUB_ENV) for secrets; avoid echo-based file writing

findings.issue: GDPR delete route does not clean up audit_logs or consent_logs — user's audit trail persists after account deletion
findings.impact: GDPR Right to Erasure partially implemented; user data remains in audit and consent tables
findings.fix: Add explicit deletion of audit_logs and consent_logs entries for the deleted user

findings.issue: No Redis container defined in production Docker compose — REDIS_URL is configured but no Redis service exists
findings.impact: Redis-dependent features (idempotency, socket adapter, rate limiting) silently fall back to in-memory mode
findings.fix: Add Redis service to docker-compose.prod.yml or document that Redis is an external managed service

findings.issue: In-memory idempotency fallback has no LRU eviction or max size — unbounded memory growth under high message volume
findings.impact: Potential OOM on burst traffic patterns
findings.fix: Add LRU eviction with max 10000 entries to in-memory Map

findings.issue: Audit event queue is in-memory with no persistence — events lost on process restart
findings.impact: Audit trail gaps during deploy/hotfix windows
findings.fix: Replace in-memory queue with Redis-backed persistent queue

findings.issue: No down/rollback scripts exist for any of 26 migrations — forward-fix is the only recovery path
findings.impact: Migration rollback requires PITR with data loss instead of simple SQL reversal
findings.fix: Write .down.sql scripts for all migrations; mandate down scripts for all future migrations

findings.issue: No distributed tracing — only basic request IDs; no OpenTelemetry span propagation across services
findings.impact: Cannot trace a single user action across API -> DB -> WebSocket -> webhook
findings.fix: Add OpenTelemetry for Express, Supabase queries, and outbound HTTP calls

findings.issue: Frontend has no structured logging — console.log/error used ad-hoc with no format
findings.impact: Client-side errors cannot be diagnosed from logs
findings.fix: Add frontend logging library with remote log shipping for production errors

findings.issue: Feature flag service uses getSupabaseAdmin() for ALL operations including reads — bypasses RLS
findings.impact: Overprivileged data access pattern; RLS cannot restrict feature flag reads
findings.fix: Use req.supabase for reads, getSupabaseAdmin() only for writes

findings.issue: No E2E test for the core auth flow (magic link -> callback -> workspace redirect) — all auth tests stubbed/skipped
findings.impact: Cannot detect auth flow regressions in CI — the most critical user journey is untested
findings.fix: Build Tier 1 auth scenario: mock magic link, verify callback redirect, validate session persistence, test workspace list render

findings.issue: No E2E test for workspace create, channel create, or message send flow — core product journey untested
findings.impact: Cannot detect regressions in the primary user action sequence in CI
findings.fix: Build Tier 1 product scenario: create workspace -> create channel -> send message -> verify message appears

findings.issue: No E2E test for cross-tenant isolation — user A cannot see user B's data
findings.impact: Cannot detect tenant isolation regressions — a single regression could expose all data across workspaces
findings.fix: Build Tier 2 authorization scenario: user A creates workspace and data, user B attempts to access — verify 403

findings.issue: No E2E test for message edit and delete workflows
findings.impact: Cannot detect regressions in message update/delete UX
findings.fix: Build Tier 1 messaging scenario: send message -> edit content -> verify update; send -> delete -> verify removal

findings.issue: No E2E test for file upload (image + document)
findings.impact: Upload path regressions undetected until production
findings.fix: Build Tier 2 file upload scenario: upload image, verify preview; upload document, verify download link

findings.issue: No E2E test for real-time message delivery between two browser contexts
findings.impact: Core realtime feature — multi-user message delivery untested in CI
findings.fix: Build Tier 2 realtime scenario: two browser contexts, one sends message, verify other receives it via WebSocket

findings.issue: No E2E test for WebSocket reconnect behavior after disconnect
findings.impact: Reconnect logic untested — messages could be lost during disconnect window
findings.fix: Build Tier 2 reconnect scenario: disconnect socket, reconnect, verify room membership restored and no messages lost

findings.issue: 54 E2E test stubs exist in comprehensive.spec.ts but all are test.skip — effectively zero E2E coverage
findings.impact: 48 test cases defined but none execute in CI; false sense of coverage
findings.fix: Prioritize un-skipping auth, workspace, and message tests with proper test data seeding

findings.issue: No test data factories or fixture files — all test data inlined per test file
findings.impact: Brittle tests; any schema change requires updating multiple test files
findings.fix: Create shared test data factories for users, workspaces, channels, messages

findings.issue: Two Playwright configs exist but only root config (chromium-only) runs in CI — apps/web/e2e/ config with 3 browsers unused
findings.impact: Firefox and WebKit E2E coverage never tested in CI
findings.fix: Consolidate to single Playwright config or add multi-browser execution in CI

findings.issue: Worker package has no test script at all — zero test coverage
findings.impact: Background worker failures undetected by CI
findings.fix: Add vitest configuration and basic worker logic tests

findings.issue: All 20+ Playwright test scenarios are prefixed with test.skip — zero executable E2E coverage
findings.impact: The entire E2E suite is disabled. No auth flow, workspace creation, messaging, or any user journey is tested in CI or locally. Regressions in critical paths (login callback, workspace redirect, message send/receive) go completely undetected.
findings.fix: Remove test.skip prefixes. Implement proper test user provisioning (Supabase MFA bypass or test credentials). Add CI E2E job with Supabase local or Docker-based test environment.

findings.issue: E2E tests depend on hardcoded test user UUIDs and workspace slugs that may not exist in test environments
findings.impact: Tests assume specific user IDs (e.g., '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001') and workspace slugs that must be pre-seeded. Without a test data setup script or fixture, tests will fail in any fresh environment including CI.
findings.fix: Add a test data seeding script (e.g., scripts/e2e-seed.ts) that creates users, workspaces, and channels before test execution. Reference dynamically-created IDs rather than hardcoded values.

findings.issue: No E2E tests for message sending, editing, deletion, reactions, threads, or file uploads
findings.impact: The core product feature — messaging — has zero E2E coverage. Critical user flows like send message, edit message, delete message, add reaction, create thread reply, and upload file are never tested end-to-end.

findings.issue: E2E test execution is not wired into any CI workflow
findings.impact: Even when tests become executable, they only run locally. PRs and pushes to develop/main do not execute any E2E tests. Regressions in critical user flows can be merged and deployed without detection.
findings.fix: Add E2E job to validate.yml (called by ci.yml). Use a Docker-based Supabase test environment or Supabase local CLI. Run smoke tier tests on every push and full suite nightly or pre-release.

findings.issue: Dev livekit turn domain hardcoded to 'localhost'; prod livekit uses DOMAIN env var (chat.mainecybertech.com)
